title: With SynchCommit=0 (the tested setting, IRIS default) an acknowledged ledger commit can be lost on an instance crash
intended: A revision the ledger reports as committed exists afterwards (spec 213: a revision exists iff its mutations are visible; clients treat the returned revision as durable). No IVG document states a durability premise or the IRIS setting it needs.
observed: Live: with iris.cpf SynchCommit=0 (the IRIS default: TCOMMIT returns before the journal is synced), a 36,000-operation commit acknowledged as seq 3 was entirely absent after a SIGKILL of the container and journal recovery; the ledger stayed consistent (head, revision rows, statement/tuple map, verify equal) and a retry with the same idempotency key committed once. The in-flight trial recovered all-or-nothing.
remedy: Document the durability premise (SynchCommit=1 or a journal flush before acknowledging, or say that acknowledged revisions can be lost on a crash and that an idempotent retry recovers them), and consider checking the setting at enable().
notes: Attributed to the tested IRIS configuration SynchCommit=0 (iris.cpf of the audit container).Environment premise rather than a code defect: the engine's documented default permits it. Exactly-once is preserved by the idempotency key; durability is not. The earlier run live-crash-world-r1-invalid exercised two crash/restart cycles without a commit in flight. Review-response reclassification (review R2-08 / R-11, condition 5; 2026-11-14): disposition changed from reproduced-live to intent-undecided, as the review asks. The record itself says no IVG document states a durability premise or the IRIS setting it needs, and calls it an environment premise; spec 213's 'a revision exists iff its mutations are visible' does not say across an instance crash.The premise is recorded in TRUST.md (durability needs SynchCommit=1 or a journal flush before acknowledging). Conditional on the maintainer's durability statement (STATUS residual question 7). Repeated (steer 10-11, incidents/SYNCHCOMMIT-WORLDS.md): under SynchCommit=0 an acknowledged commit was lost in 3 of 3 trials (live-crash-repeat-sc0); under SynchCommit=1 in 0 of 3 (live-crash-repeat-sc1; the container was restored to 0). The loss is attributable to the SynchCommit=0 setting; three trials are evidence, not proof that SynchCommit=1 suffices. Observed behaviour kept and still live: with SynchCommit=0 (env-synchcommit-setting) an acknowledged commit was absent after SIGKILL and journal recovery (live-crash-world-r2, one trial; repeated 3 of 3 in live-crash-repeat-sc0).
